dod_intent_evidence: Homepage banner reads 'Backed by DoD' and links 'How it is used by the Army' (own-words section); News section shows a Nov 2023 SOCOM Phase III SBIR award ('improved situational awareness and combat effectiveness') and a NAVAIR/NAWCAD R&D contract.
score_evidence: 'Pison continuously learns your unique nervous system to predict your cognitive performance 24/7' → lab_language_intensity (algorithmic/real-time brag, zero operational framing)
Entire site never mentions DDIL, ATO, RMF, CMMC, ITAR, STIG, or SWaP-C despite claiming 'Backed by DoD' → deployment_awareness_absence maxed
'operators' appears only as 'For owners, operators & decision-makers' — a business-exec audience label, not a military operator, training, or CONOPS reference anywhere → operator_absence
no jobs data found in pack → hiring_profile_skew set to 10 per instructions

founded 2016 (10 years), 81 employees, ~$17M disclosed funding, and the company's primary current public product is a $29/mo consumer wearable subscription rather than a defense product → stage_pressure (a decade-old company monetizing via consumer wellness suggests the defense business hasn't sustained it alone)

blind_spots.blind_spot: No mention of TAK/ATAK anywhere despite defense-side work integrating gesture control into AFSOC tactical-awareness systems.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A neural/gesture signal has to land inside an operator's existing TAK kit to be useful in a mission — the consumer site's total silence on this integration path is the same 'nobody built the adapter' gap that stalls transitions.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Public-facing product messaging has pivoted entirely to consumer cognitive-performance wellness; the tactical integration work lives only in SBIR/contract records, not brand language.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: 'The Pison Platform provides real-time insights into your cognitive state, time-of-day patterns, lifestyle impacts and long-term trends.'

blind_spots.blind_spot: Zero discussion of ruggedization, battery endurance, or wear-under-gloves/NVGs despite claiming 'passive tracking of nerve signals... day and night' for a device implicitly marketed toward operators.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A consumer fitness-watch chassis and battery are not built for continuous wear under a SOF operator's kit, gloves, or field conditions — SWaP-C constraints on a mission-relevant biosensor are a different engineering problem than a $29/mo wellness product.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Product engineering appears optimized for consumer comfort/battery-life expectations (daily charging, athletic use), not field endurance.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: 'Wear it — Passive tracking of nerve signals, heart rate, sleep, and motion. Day and night.'

blind_spots.blind_spot: No ATO/RMF/ITAR language despite a SOCOM press release describing the technology as feeding 'improved situational awareness and combat effectiveness.'
blind_spots.operator_reality: Biometric/neural telemetry destined for a combat-effectiveness use case is exactly the kind of personnel data that needs an accreditation and data-handling story before it touches a program of record — nothing in the company's own language addresses this.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The company's public voice is entirely consumer-product marketing; compliance/accreditation topics don't fit that register and aren't visible anywhere.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: 'Phase III Small Business Innovation Research contract will integrate Pison's neural biosensing and AI technology for improved situational awareness and combat effectiveness'

opener_hook: SOCOM's Phase III SBIR tasked Pison with 'combat effectiveness' integration in Nov 2023, but pison.com today sells a $29/mo consumer wellness watch — how's the tactical-side ATO tracking?
what_they_do: Neural/ENG wristband sensing platform, sold publicly as a consumer cognitive-performance wearable, with parallel DoD SBIR work on gesture-control and situational-awareness integration.
